# Encodes the definition's necessary conditions as boolean features per option,
# then derives which options satisfy ALL of them. The features are a judgment-based
# reading of the text, not a computed fact, so this is rule application over that reading.

options = {
    # recipient_is_distinct_from_provider, recipient_contributes_own_resource,
    # improves_service_level_jointly, win_win_for_both
    "A": dict(distinct=True,  contributes=True,  improves_service=False, win_win=False),
    # A: parents work free; school saves money, but no service improvement and no clear gain for parents
    "B": dict(distinct=True,  contributes=True,  improves_service=True,  win_win=True),
    # B: customers bring stools (resource), service feels better, sales rise: both gain
    "C": dict(distinct=False, contributes=True,  improves_service=False, win_win=False),
    # C: no provider/recipient relationship (does own housework)
    "D": dict(distinct=True,  contributes=True,  improves_service=False, win_win=True),
    # D: motive is corporate image; customers' bags are not used to improve the service level
}

def qualifies(f):
    return all(f.values())

derived = sorted(k for k, f in options.items() if qualifies(f))
submitted = ["B", "D"]

for k, f in options.items():
    failed = [n for n, v in f.items() if not v]
    print(k, "qualifies" if qualifies(f) else "fails on " + ", ".join(failed))

print("Derived set:", derived)
print("Submitted set:", submitted)
print("CHECK PASS" if derived == sorted(submitted) else "CHECK FAIL")
